completion_data.completion_summary: Landed the Determinism clause of app:presheaf-dictionary as a theorem pair: deterministic_iff_separated states F.Deterministic iff every restriction map of Beh(F) is injective at a regular frame, and separated_strictly_stronger shows separatedness is strictly stronger than the validity of Determined on the frame, refuted at the repository's own drift frame F-zero. Split across the Presheaf/ cluster's assert_not_exists layering lock into three files, with all four plan phases closed green at lake build FormalSystem exit 0, zero sorries, and ALL CHECKS PASSED on the module-invariant gate set.

memory_candidates.content: In BimodalLogic, a Semantics/Presheaf/ cluster module cannot name TaskFrame.SingletonClasses: that name is declared in Semantics/DeterministicBridge.lean, which transitively imports FormalSystem.ProofSystem.Axioms via PlusDeterminism -> PlusValidity -> Validity -> ValidityLayer -> FrameClassValidity, so importing it breaks the cluster's closing 'assert_not_exists FormalSystem.ProofSystem.Axiom FormalSystem.ProofSystem.DerivationTree'. The sanctioned pattern is to state the content with the name UNFOLDED inside the cluster and attach the name in a one-line repackaging above the lock -- the same split the tree already uses for states_eq_of_deterministic (choice-free, PlusDeterminism.lean) versus deterministic_of_singletonClasses (ZFC, DeterministicBridge.lean). Semantics/FrameProperty.lean, by contrast, IS lock-compatible (it carries only Semantics/TaskFrame.lean plus two Mathlib order files), so TaskFrame.Deterministic can be imported into the cluster directly.

Adding one .lean file to BimodalLogic requires four mechanical regenerations beyond the module itself, and skipping any of them fails a gate rather than merely looking untidy: (1) one import line in the directory's sibling aggregator; (2) 'lake exe mk_all --lib FormalSystem' for the root FormalSystem.lean (C33 is byte-for-byte; note mk_all EXITS 1 when it rewrites the file, which is success, not failure); (3) 'bash scripts/check-module-invariants.sh --emit-inventory' for every README generated-inventory block, then hand-write the new row's description (the generator writes '<!-- TODO: add description -->' and PRESERVES a hand-written description across later re-emits, so re-emit freely); (4) 'bash scripts/typst-sync-check.sh --fix' plus staging typst/generated/status.typ -- a pre-commit hook BLOCKS the commit on stale file/line counts. Steps 3 and 4 must be re-run after any later edit that changes the module's line count, including a docstring-only pass.

When a plan pins an axiom profile from a research probe, re-measure it in-tree rather than transcribing it: a probe's declaration can measure differently from the library declaration it becomes, because the probe's own import set differs. Here driftSec was pinned [propext, Quot.sound] from a draft reading but measures [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] in the library module, the choice arriving ambiently through driftLinear. Measure with a scratch file ('import <Module>' then '#print axioms <FullyQualified.name>') run under 'lake env lean', which is far cheaper than a build and gives the exact list to paste into the docstring.

reflection.what_worked: Transcribing from the research probe rather than re-deriving: every proof term compiled first try, and the only two corrections were an import and an axiom pin, both caught by the scoped build before any full build was spent. Running a scoped 'lake build <Module>' before each full build turned a ~9-minute feedback loop into a ~90-second one.
reflection.what_was_hard: The repo's generated-artifact surface. A new .lean file induces edits in four generated files (root aggregator, three README inventories, typst status counts), and the typst one is enforced by a pre-commit hook that only fires at commit time -- so the first commit attempt was blocked after all verification had already passed. The slow tail of a full build (four modules over 100s each, past job 2790) also made each phase-end verification cost most of its wall time in modules unrelated to the change.
reflection.what_was_missed: That the plan's Phase 1 import list was incomplete was not caught by reading the plan against the probe; it surfaced only at elaboration. Reading the probe's imports against the planned module's imports and diffing which declarations each supplies would have caught it before the first build.
reflection.successes: All four phases closed green and committed individually, all 11 declared identifiers landed at their intended sites with the plan's exact signatures, all six pinned axiom profiles matched measurement exactly, and the Scope Hypotheses were each confirmed by probe rather than assumed -- including Phase 3's transitive-import claim, which held.
